title: Imagine walking into that room.
paragraphs: Imagine walking into that room.
The disciples were arguing about greatness.

Who would be the greatest in the kingdom?
Who would sit closest to the throne?
Then something unexpected happened.
Jesus stood up.
He wrapped a towel around His waist.
He poured water into a basin.
And one by one, the Son of God knelt in front of His disciples and washed the dust from their feet.
Even Judas.
The one who would betray Him in just a few hours.
That moment reveals something powerful about the kingdom of God.
God measures greatness differently.

Not by power.
Not by position.
Not by recognition.
But by humility.
Jesus did not just teach humility.
He demonstrated it.
The King knelt.
The Lord served.
The Savior washed feet.
And in doing so, He left us a lesson that still challenges every generation:
True greatness is not about how many people serve you.
It is about how many people you are willing to serve.
Because the heart of God is not only seen on a throne.
It is seen in a Savior holding a towel.
